title: Exact normalized recurrence and adversarial evidence for the actual c=1 gap
mathematical_status: exact chamber identities plus finite adversarial evidence; universal sign lemma open

notation.macaulay_upper: U_d(N) is the d-th Macaulay upper shadow: if N=sum_i binom(t_i,i) is its canonical d-binomial expansion, then U_d(N)=sum_i binom(t_i,i+1).
notation.actual_c1_parameters: For c=1 write b=q+k and u=r+k-1. The dyadic equation is (k-1)q+binom(k-1,2)+2-r=2h, with h=112*2^(j-1).

first_normalization.common_form: On either target chamber write x=binom(a,3)+alpha and y=binom(a+1,3)+beta, with 0<=alpha<binom(a,2) and 0<=beta<binom(a+1,2).
first_normalization.target_condition: The arrow target ++ is exactly p>=0 and v>=0.

two_row_recurrence.definition: Set A_0=alpha, B_0=beta and, whenever both new tails are nonnegative, A_(s+1)=U_(s+2)(A_s)-tau+1 and B_(s+1)=U_(s+2)(B_s)-tau.
two_row_recurrence.borrow_caveat: If P<0 or V<0, the displayed no-borrow gamma6 formula is not valid. This does not obstruct a row already recovered by gamma5>=0; any proof that reaches rank six must split this sign wall explicitly.

piecewise_polynomial_realization.coordinate_rule: On a fixed Macaulay chamber, introduce canonical coordinates N=sum_(i=1)^d binom(t_i,i), t_d>...>t_1>=0. Then U_d(N)=sum_(i=1)^d binom(t_i,i+1), so every displayed recurrence is an explicit binomial polynomial in the chamber coordinates.
piecewise_polynomial_realization.gamma5_cell: If alpha=sum_(i=1)^2 binom(a_i,i), p=sum_(i=1)^3 binom(p_i,i), and v=sum_(i=1)^3 binom(v_i,i), then gamma5=sum_(i=1)^3[binom(v_i,i+1)-binom(p_i,i+1)]-sum_(i=1)^2 binom(a_i,i+1)-1.
piecewise_polynomial_realization.gamma6_cell: If P=sum_(i=1)^4 binom(P_i,i) and V=sum_(i=1)^4 binom(V_i,i), then gamma6=sum_(i=1)^4[binom(V_i,i+1)-binom(P_i,i+1)]-sum_(i=1)^3 binom(p_i,i+1)-1.
piecewise_polynomial_realization.interpretation: The remaining proof problem is a finite-pattern inequality problem only after the order relations among these chamber coordinates have been exhaustively partitioned; the formulas alone do not establish their signs.

strongest_supported_invariant.candidate: For every actual c=1 state in either (++ -> ++) or (-- -> ++) with gamma4<0: gamma5>=0, or else P>=0, V>=0, and gamma6>=0.
strongest_supported_invariant.equivalent_recovery_claim: max(gamma5,gamma6)>=0, with rank six invoked only in the gamma5<0 branch.
strongest_supported_invariant.why_this_form: The earliest actual (++ -> ++) state has P<0 but gamma5=89319>0. All adversarial gamma5-negative states found are (-- -> ++) states with P,V>=0 and positive gamma6.

r_strategy: 49 divisibility-compatible probes around the A=0 first-tail sign wall for every (j,k)

observed_gamma5_negative_region.comment: Author-search domain only. Independent audit extended the box and found gamma5-negative states at least through k=43,r=133 by j=40, so this concentration is not stable and must not be used for a finite-fibre reduction.

adversarial_search.interpretation: No counterexample to the candidate invariant was found. This is adversarial finite evidence, not exhaustive in unbounded r and not a proof. The search harness was repaired after independent audit so gamma5<0 with P<0 or V<0 is counted as a failure rather than silently skipped.

proof_obligations: Prove gamma5>=0 throughout the actual (++ -> ++) chamber, including all Macaulay subchambers, or exhibit and repair a negative subchamber.
In the actual (-- -> ++) chamber prove that gamma5<0 forces P,V>=0 and gamma6>=0; the known fixed-(k,r) family is only one subfamily.
Do not assume bounded k and r: the independent audit disproved stability of the original k<=17,r<=46 search box. Seek a scale-uniform chamber inequality instead.
Exhaust the Macaulay coordinate order types needed by the two explicit cell polynomials; do not infer universality from the bounded search.

bounded_guard.result: 2392996 parameter triples tested; 46018 target states accepted; no gamma5/gamma6 double-negative state and no gamma5-negative rank-six-borrow state. Independent wider audit found the negative k,r box grows with scale.
